extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients and institutional eRA Commons users (principal investigators, administrative staff, grant administrators) responsible for closeout reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting the Final Research Performance Progress Report (Final RPPR) and Interim RPPR as part of NIH grant closeout using eRA Commons, including when each report is required and how Interim RPPRs are treated if a Type 2 renewal is under consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR required at closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Research Performance Progress Report (Final RPPR) is one of three reports required as part of the closeout process for the end of an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Final RPPR must be submitted when closing out an award; it is a mandatory component of the award closeout process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions triggering a Final RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: A Final RPPR is required for any grant that is terminated and any award that will not be extended through award of a new competitive segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an award ends prematurely (termination) or the institution will not receive a new competitive segment to extend the award, the institution must submit a Final RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim RPPR required when a Type 2 renewal is submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If a competitive renewal (Type 2) application has been submitted, the recipient must submit an Interim RPPR while their renewal application is under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit an Interim RPPR during the period the Type 2 application is pending to provide current performance information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of the Interim RPPR depending on renewal outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Type 2 is funded, NIH will treat the Interim RPPR as the annual performance report for the final year of the previous competitive segment. If the Type 2 is not funded, the Interim RPPR will be treated by NIH staff as the institution's Final RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that the Interim RPPR may effectively serve as either an annual report or the Final RPPR depending on the award renewal decision; prepare content accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must be logged into eRA Commons with appropriate role(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be logged into eRA Commons with appropriate role(s) to complete these activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only users with the requisite eRA Commons roles and privileges can access, edit, and submit RPPRs. Refer to 'eRA Commons Roles & Privileges At a Glance' for role mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine which grants require closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic task: Determine which grants require closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional records and NIH systems to identify awards reaching end of project period, terminated awards, or awards not being extended; this is a prerequisite step before preparing RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: View grant closeout requirements under Closeout Status
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic task: View grant closeout requirements under Closeout Status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Closeout Status screen in eRA Commons to see specific closeout actions required for each grant (e.g., final reports, property reports, invoices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow RPPR submission procedures (Interim and Final)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic task: Submitting Your Interim Research Performance Progress Report and Submitting Your Final Research Performance Progress Report (step-by-step instructions available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online help step-by-step instructions and use the RPPR form (e.g., Section A, Cover Page and navigation tabs) to complete and submit reports; screenshots and form navigation examples are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use RPPR Instruction Guide and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional Resources include the RPPR Instruction Guide, RPPR Resources Page, Grants Closeout FAQs, Research Performance Progress Report web page, and 'Overview of the Interim RPPR' and 'RPPR: Who Can Do What?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these resources for detailed instructions, examples, role responsibilities, and answers to common questions when preparing Interim or Final RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with NIH policies and notices regarding closeout and RPPRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy references: NIH Grants Policy Statement: Closeout; NIH Grants Policy Statement: Final Progress Report; NIH Guide Notice NOT-OD-17-037: NIH Implementation of the Interim-RPPR While a Renewal Application is Under Consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure RPPR content and timing adhere to NIH Grants Policy Statement requirements and specific NIH notices (e.g., NOT-OD-17-037) regarding how Interim RPPRs are handled during renewal consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eRA interface aids (Status Result screen and RPPR form screenshots)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual guidance: Main Screenshots include the Status Result screen showing how to access the RPPR to edit information and the RPPR form, section A, Cover Page and navigation tabs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the provided screenshots to locate the RPPR in eRA Commons and understand form navigation when editing and completing the report.
